Search terms for this lesson“how do I combine reused hazards and phases into readable boss patterns?”Outline only

Your arena stands, and the boss takes hits from both E and Space. Today you layer in attack patterns by reusing the hazards already inside Assets/Scripts/ — then run a Self-Playtest to try beating your own fight before handing the controller to a friend.

Break It Down~10 minOutline only

Combine reused hazards into readable boss attack waves and a Phase 2 shift, then self-playtest honestly.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Reuse TurretController, Spawner, and Platform as phase-driven boss partswhat does this part do?Read: 3.1–3.4 (TurretController.timeBetweenShots, "E_Fireball") and Platform.isOn in 6.3
  2. Switch attack timings or activate extra hazards when health dropswhat does this part do?Read: 8.2 (phaseTwo threshold inside ChangeHealth()) & Enemy State Machines doc

A boss does not need 300 lines of custom AI math to feel tense. Mounting two TurretController prefabs that wake up in Phase 2, starting a moving Platform lift (isOn = true), or cutting timeBetweenShots in half reuses tested scripts while dramatically changing how the player moves through the arena.

Your turn

Pick two of the parts above and say in one line what each one actually does.

Look at Projectile.cs and PlayerController.cs: any object tagged "E_Fireball" deals -2 HP on trigger enter. Why can your boss reuse "E_Fireball" hazard orbs or turrets right away without modifying PlayerController?

In your self-playtest today, what is the difference between a pattern that is hard (fair telegraph, avoidable once learned) and a pattern that is cheap (unavoidable overlapping hits)?

In the Code + Editor: Build Two Phases Out of Reused Parts (~35 min) ~35 min

Pick two hazard or arena changes that trigger when your boss enters Phase 2 (health <= maxHealth / 2):

Reused ToolHow to Wire It Into the BossHow Phase 2 Changes It
TurretController + Projectile Child turrets on the boss or corner walls tracking target (or fixed spawn angles) with timeBetweenShots = 2.0f. Drop timeBetweenShots to 1.1f or call SetActive(true) on a second corner turret.
EnemyController Boss patrols patrolPoints across the arena at speed = 2. Double speed to 4 or tighten aggro speed when enraged.
Platform + Spawner Static platform at rest (isOn = false), or periodic wave spawn via Instantiate(). Flip platform.isOn = true; when Phase 2 starts or trigger a single minion wave via Spawner logic.
Do NOT spawn an infinite wall of minions or bullets every frame. Calling Instantiate() inside Update() without checking a cooldown timer (timer -= Time.deltaTime) freezes Unity cleanly in two seconds. Guard every spawn with a reset timer just like TurretController.cs does.

Socratic: Combining Existing Systems

  1. If a boss activates a child Turret in Phase 2 using phaseTwoTurret.SetActive(true);, why must you start that object inactive in the Scene Hierarchy — and reset it cleanly if the scene reloads?
  2. PlayerController.OnTriggerEnter2D() subtracts -2 HP on "E_Fireball", while StatManager.maxHealth is 3. How many fireballs can a player survive in one fight, and what happens if two hit in the same second?
  3. Why does giving the player a brief breather window (or resetting cooldownTimer cleanly between attacks) make a fight more strategic than constant random firing?
Studio Check: Self-Playtest Protocol (~25 min) ~25 min

Before asking a friend to test tomorrow, try beating your own boss three times in a row playing honestly (do not walk around bugs or dodge spots only you know about):

Run #Style UsedResult (Win / HP Left)Top Fairness / Timing Issue Found
1Melee focus (KeyCode.E)
2Ranged focus (KeyCode.Space)
3Mixed + double jumps + platforms

Socratic: Designing for Players Who Do Not Know Your Code

  1. In your self-playtest, which strategy won way too easily (e.g., standing safely in a corner firing Space forever)? What single tweak closes that cheese?
  2. Compare beating your boss with melee versus ranged: did one feel useless, or did both create interesting risk/reward?
  3. Write down one visual cue you need to add tomorrow if an attack currently comes out too fast to dodge on reaction.

Socratic: Pattern Timing

  1. Look at timeBetweenShots across all active turrets in Phase 2: if two turrets fire on identical 1.5f timers, do they shoot in sync forever or stagger cleanly?
  2. If the player loses all health during Phase 2 and StatManager.Die() reloads the scene, verify every Phase 2 object starts back in Phase 1 rather than staying enraged.
  3. Name the single biggest fix from your self-playtest table that you will apply before friend playtesting next class.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Reuse turrets, moving platforms, spawners, or patrol speeds inside a working Phase 1 → Phase 2 fight
  • Guard every projectile/minion spawn with a cooldown timer
  • Self-playtest all three combat styles (melee, ranged, mixed) and log unfair spots honestly
  • Commit and push
